clue.text: Exhortation to husband

parts.note: to husband resources is to use them sparingly, and the proverb urging thrift is the exhortation meant

explanation.surface: A wife urges her husband to do something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a noun, the target of the exhortation, but it is the verb meaning to conserve or economise.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb is a call to thrift, urging people to conserve resources, which is what husbanding them means.

clue.text: Where one may stay dry

parts.note: dry here means free of alcohol, not out of the rain: a lodging that served no drink

explanation.surface: Somewhere to shelter from the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: A temperance hotel was a Victorian-era hotel that served no alcohol; 'dry' means teetotal, not sheltered.
explanation.definitionFit: Such hotels were run by the teetotal movement and served no alcoholic drink, so guests stayed dry in the abstaining sense.

clue.text: Bag holds writhing viper in agitated state

indicators.note: the first word holds the scrambled letters within it, a container signal

parts.note: to bag something is to get or fetch it

indicators.note: a writhing snake twists about, so its letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bag contains a squirming snake, causing panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' looks like a noun but is the verb, to fetch; 'holds' splits it to take in the anagram that 'writhing' makes of VIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is a state of intense excitement or agitation, an idiom drawn from a high temperature.

clue.text: Lift most of the secrecy

parts.note: to lift is slang for to steal

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter, keeping the opening run

explanation.surface: Someone lifts nearly all the secret material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the last letter of THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is furtive, covert action, a close synonym of secrecy.

clue.text: Beaten by a single stroke

parts.note: in tennis a player beaten by a serve they cannot touch has been beaten by one stroke, an ace

explanation.surface: A golfer loses a match by one shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By a single stroke' suggests a narrow golf defeat; it means defeated outright by one unreturnable serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aced in tennis is to be beaten by a serve so good the receiver cannot touch it.

clue.text: The last thing one expects from an orator

definitions.text: The last thing one expects from an orator

parts.words: The last thing one expects from an orator
parts.note: read literally, the final speech a public speaker gives on leaving office or the stage

explanation.surface: Something no one would expect a speaker to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing one expects' is an idiom for something surprising; here it literally means a final speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A valedictory speech is the final one delivered by a departing figure, literally an orator's last offering.

clue.text: When robbers start or finish work?

definitions.text: When robbers start or finish work?

parts.words: When robbers start or finish work?
parts.note: knocking off is slang both for stopping work and for stealing, so robbers knock off in both senses

explanation.surface: A question about the working hours of thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock off' means both to steal and to stop work for the day, so the robbers' start and finish coincide.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking-off time is the hour work ends for the day, and knocking off is also slang for thieving.

clue.text: Such artists colour flags

parts.note: flags are paving stones, and street artists who chalk pictures on them have a name taken from where they work

explanation.surface: Artists paint national flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' are flagstones, not banners; pavement artists draw in chalk on the paving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavement artists draw pictures in chalk on paving slabs, so the paved walkway is where they colour flagstones.

clue.text: Crack outside right is cautious

indicators.note: the word for cautious sits outside the letter, wrapping around it

parts.note: canny means shrewd and careful, so to be canny is to be cautious

explanation.surface: A footballer playing outside right is careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside right' looks like a football position, but 'outside' is the container signal placing R inside CANNY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small narrow opening, a synonym for a crack or chink.

clue.text: Principal can make a good man turn pale

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: to turn here is to change about, so the letters of pale are reordered

explanation.surface: A head teacher can make a decent fellow go white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like a noun (a head teacher) but is the adjective, main; 'turn' signals the anagram of PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective staple means chief or main, as in a staple food, a synonym for principal.

clue.text: Interview everybody in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a formal meeting with an important person
the spectators gathered to watch a performance

explanation.surface: Questioning the whole crowd at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a formal hearing granted by a dignitary and the assembled spectators at a play.

clue.text: A return to divorce city — a heavy blow

indicators.note: a return means going back, so the city's name is read backwards

parts.note: Reno, Nevada was famous for its quick divorces

explanation.surface: Going back to Reno after a divorce hits hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno, in Nevada, was long known for quick, easy divorces.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for a single knockout punch, one heavy blow.

clue.text: Spare site I developed, providing party fare

indicators.note: a site that is developed is built up and transformed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A vacant plot is built on to supply food for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' signals an anagram of SPARE SITE I.
explanation.definitionFit: Patisserie means pastries and cakes, the sort of food served at a party.

clue.text: Crispbread put out for sea creature

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A cracker is set out as food for a sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' signals an anagram of CRISPBREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The spider crab is a long-legged marine crustacean, an example of a sea creature.

clue.text: Reason may follow this order to prepare for action

definitions.meaning: the phrase completed by reason is the idiom meaning to be logical
a military command telling troops to be ready for attack

explanation.surface: A logical command readying soldiers for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the start of the idiom about being logical and a military command to take up battle positions.

clue.text: Convict surrounded by a stack of booty

indicators.note: the first word is surrounded by the second, which goes round it

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A prisoner sits amid a heap of stolen loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convict' is a noun here, LAG, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage is goods taken by plunder, a synonym for booty or loot.

clue.text: One who enjoys being patronised

parts.note: patronised usually means talked down to, but here it means supported by a patron

explanation.surface: Someone who oddly likes being condescended to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronised' suggests condescension; it means having a patron who sponsors you.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is a person guided and supported by an influential patron.

clue.text: Assume responsibility and accept payment

definitions.meaning: to take control of a situation
read literally, to receive a fee or charge

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a job and gets paid for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for taking control, and literally means taking a fee.

clue.text: No good at making pudding

definitions.meaning: British slang for worthless or useless
a ... is a boiled pudding, as in plum ...

explanation.surface: Someone is hopeless at making desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum duff is a traditional British boiled suet pudding with dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff is British slang for useless and also an old name for a boiled flour pudding.

clue.text: Was prominent among people who refused to yield?

definitions.meaning: those who held out against pressure stood firm in resistance

explanation.surface: Someone noticeable within a stubborn group.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means was conspicuous and also held out, refusing to give in.

clue.text: Ring New York Times? It will be expensive

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
the multiplication sign looks like X

explanation.surface: A ring advertised in the New York Times will cost a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York Times' reads as the newspaper, but it splits into NY and Times, the sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded semi-precious stone, so a piece of it is something costly.

clue.text: Copper to reprimand one coming between vicar and his flock

definitions.text: one coming between vicar and his flock

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold or reprimand

explanation.surface: A policeman scolds someone meddling in a parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but gives CU, the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant cleric who ranks below the vicar, standing between him and the congregation.

clue.text: Winning smash volley

indicators.note: to smash is to shatter, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player wins with a smashed volley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' and 'smash' look like tennis talk; 'Winning' means charming, and 'smash' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning in the sense of charming or attractive is a synonym for delightful and pleasing.

clue.text: Pleased to prepare dog's meal

indicators.note: preparing food means making it up from its parts, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone happy to make the dog's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to prepare' signals an anagram of DOGS MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladsome is a literary word for joyful or cheerful, close in sense to pleased.
